notes:
{琴|こと} is a traditional Japanese stringed instrument, often called a "Japanese harp" in English. It is one of Japan's most iconic musical instruments.

CHARACTERISTICS:
- 13 strings stretched over movable bridges (⟦{柱|じ}→柱：noentry⟧)
- About 180 cm long, made of paulownia wood (⟦{桐|きり}→桐：noentry⟧)
- Played by plucking with picks (⟦{爪|つめ}→爪：02159_tsume⟧) on thumb, index, and middle fingers

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {琴|こと}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{弾|ひ}く→弾く：02444_hiku⟧: to play the koto
- {琴|こと}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{音色|ねいろ}→音色：07422_neiro⟧: the sound/tone of a koto
- {琴|こと}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{演奏|えんそう}→演奏：01896_ensou⟧: koto performance

CULTURAL NOTE:
Strongly associated with ⟦お{正月|しょうがつ}→正月：01433_shougatsu⟧ (New Year) — koto music is commonly heard in stores and on TV during the holiday season.

RELATED INSTRUMENTS:
- ⟦{三味線|しゃみせん}→三味線：04464_shamisen⟧: shamisen (3-stringed, plucked with plectrum)
- ⟦{尺八|しゃくはち}→尺八：04465_shakuhachi⟧: shakuhachi (bamboo flute)
